title: Vaccines Are a Saved Game
idea: Vaccines train immunity with a harmless preview so memory cells can crush the real virus in hours

segments.narration: What if you could lose without getting sick?
segments.visual_directive: A red spiky virus multiplies fast, then freezes as a glowing shield slams down over it.

segments.narration: Your immune system is slow the first time it meets a new virus. It takes days to build the right antibodies. Meanwhile the virus is multiplying like crazy.
segments.visual_directive: Drifting white blood cells in a bloodstream while a day counter ticks and small red viruses double again and again.

segments.narration: A vaccine gives you a safe practice round. Say, just one harmless spike from the virus, that can't multiply. Patrol cells grab it and flash its mugshot to your lymph nodes. A matching B cell wakes up and clones itself thousands of times. Those clones pump out Y shaped antibodies that stick to the spike and block it. When the drill ends, most clones die off. But a handful stay as memory cells, on guard for years.
segments.visual_directive: A single yellow spike floats in and a patrol cell carries it to a glowing lymph node. One blue B cell clones into an army firing Y shaped antibodies that lock onto spikes.

segments.narration: So when the real virus arrives, memory cells strike in hours, not days. You're protected before you even feel sick.
segments.visual_directive: Real red viruses rush back but dormant memory cells flash awake and flood them with antibodies until they dissolve.
